video_title: ‘It’s going to be MUST-SEE TV’ 🔥 Windy is excited to watch LaMelo and Anthony Edwards | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves face salary cap constraints after acquiring LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: There's not a lot of wiggle room financially with them being hard capped now

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: Tim, this has been a very eventful week thanks to this guy to my left. You cover Minnesota for us extensively. What do you think is next? Because it feels like this is the move that they are making to build yet another team around Anthony Edwards.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Look, as Bobby laid out, there's not a lot of wiggle room financially with them being hard capped now to fill out the rest of the roster. They do have a glaring hole at power forward. It's kind of a whack-a-mole situation. You fill the glaring need at point guard, you hope with a star, and boom, you've got a need at power forward with Julius Randle gone, with Naz Reid gone. There was a Wolves source put it to me, we went from 48 minutes of outstanding power forward play to zero. Now, they likely bump Jaden McDaniels up. He'll probably play a lot of the four, playing with three guards, maybe even in that starting lineup. And then they hope to find some help at the four, kind of in the bargain bins of free agency. But again, they don't have a lot of flexibility, a lot of spending power to fill out the rest of this roster despite the fact that there is a clear-cut need.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves have exhausted their draft assets to build around Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: They are running low on draft assets and it's going to be hard to go get a power forward

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: It does feel like this is the last iteration of future assets that they can afford to put around him.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: There's basically been three cycles of the draft assets. It was the Rudy Gobert trade, right? You diminished most of it and Gobert was certainly good for you. There was the Rob Dillingham trade the night of the draft when they made that trade with San Antonio and we thought that was the end of their draft assets. And then what happens every year, it basically recycles and fills back up here. It's like filling up your gas tank here. Now they had another first-round pick in 2033 that came to life today and now that goes to Charlotte here. And yes, they are running low on draft assets and it's going to be hard to go use a draft asset or in go get a power forward. And I think you're probably looking at the trade market, you're probably looking at maybe dumping some salary here, maybe going out and exploring using your $6 million exception here. But they've got to be creative. Their front office has got to be creative as far as filling in those gaps.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Connelly's aggressive front office strategy to build around Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: Tim Connelly and their front office has made a name for himself as being unafraid

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: But that's what Shams, what you were explaining earlier on the show, is that Tim Connelly and their front office has made a name for himself as being unafraid to go take these big moves, make these big swings, and then fill out the roster and a four is really what they need.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Yeah, and they, I'm sure, have a whiteboard with targets that they're going to go after and they're going to try to pursue and try to sell in free agency to come to play for the minimum or whatever they can pay them that Bobby Marks can tell us they can pay.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves prioritize talent infusion to help Anthony Edwards win a championship
quotes.excerpt: They felt like they needed an infusion of talent. They felt like they were low on talent
quotes.quote: This is a group that they went all in now with LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, obviously Anthony Edwards. They felt like they needed an infusion of talent. They felt like they were low on talent. I spoke to a source today and my understanding is LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards, these guys are friends, they've communicated and LaMelo Ball understands the task at hand coming to Minnesota and that's trying to help Anthony Edwards win a championship there.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's career transition to a high-stakes environment in Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: LaMelo has never really played for anything with stakes. Even this year, the Hornets were a playing team
quotes.quote: LaMelo has never really played for anything with stakes. Even this year, the Hornets were a playing team. He will enter this season with stakes. He will enter this season with a highlight. He's been on national TV what, two times a year max? These guys are going to be all over the national television.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: General managers view the LaMelo Ball trade as a high-stakes gamble
quotes.excerpt: I texted several general managers a simple question, what do you think of the LaMelo deal?
quotes.quote: I texted several general managers a simple question, what do you think of the LaMelo deal? And one replied one sentence, Tim is a riverboat gambler. And this is big-time, high-stakes gambling that he's doing right here. And you understand the swing that he's taking, you understand the hole in the roster it's creating. Chris Finch is also one of the most creative coaches in the league and he's going to earn his money figuring out how to make this work.
